title: Hand-off priming and circuit-breaker cheats (evening shift)
body:
Context / goal:
Lightweight evening shift notes to prime the on-call/shift handoff for small-mid releases. Meant for quick glance: what to watch, how to pin, quick rollback triggers, who to ping. Not exhaustive — append as you learn.

Short summary of plan:
- Canary cohorts: 0.5% -> 2% -> 8% over 45m / 1h windows (small feature toggle flip).
- Traffic gating: header-based routing via X-Launch-Cohort header; SDK clients to opt-in.
- Warmup: 15m warmup at 0.5% with synthetic traffic for KV/cache priming.
- Observability: focus on P95 latency, model token error rate, RPC error ratio, tail OOMs, and cost anomalies.

Pre-launch quick checklist (5–10m run):
- [ ] Confirm image tag pinned in rollout config (deploy-config: image: runtime:v2025-11-04-rc3).
- [ ] Canary route rule updated in traffic router (router: canary-rules/latest).
- [ ] Canary healthchecks green for last 3 autoscaling cycles (svc/canary-health).
- [ ] Alert silencing: ensure noisy integration alerts are suppressed for 1h window (alert: infra/noise-adjust).
- [ ] Slack relay: #deploys-evening + oncall DM route set (oncall: ravi).
- [ ] Notify the three product owners and list clients with expected changes (Maya/Oliver).

Warmup and priming notes:
- Start synthetic priming at t0 for 15m using priming script (scripts/priming/kv_spinup.py). Focus on common prefixes.
- If prefix cache hit-rate < 70% after 15m, extend warmup another 10m and move to 1% cohort only.
- Watch GPU memory churn — the runtime sometimes spills with long prompts during warmup. If stable, proceed.

Observability queries to run during rollout (copy to Grafana):
- Latency (P95) by model: sum by(model) (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])))
- Token error rate: increase in model_token_errors / tokens_total over 5m
- RPC error ratio: rate(rpc_errors_total[1m]) / rate(rpc_requests_total[1m])
- Pod OOM spikes: increase(kube_pod_container_oom_total[10m])
- Cost burn (approx): token_cost_estimate_per_minute inferred from token counters (dashboard tile: cost/quick)

Primary rollback / circuit-breaker triggers (auto + manual):
- Auto rollback (immediate): sustained RPC error ratio > 2% for 3 consecutive 1m buckets while canary > 0.5%
- Auto rollback (safety): P95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m and error ratio > 0.5%
- Manual rollback triggers (notify and evaluate): sudden model_token_errors spike (>5x baseline), OOMs > 1 in canary pool in 10m, or traffic divergence > 25% from expected routing (router logs)
- Circuit-breaker actions: first step scale down canary to 0.5% and pause progression; second step route all traffic off to fallback model variant v2025-10-stable and alert SRE.

Handoff script for evening on-call (what to say in 3 sentences):
- "We just kicked off a small canary for runtime:v2025-11-04-rc3 — cohorts 0.5->2->8 over 1h. Watch P95, RPC error ratio, token error spikes; queries are on the Deploy Canary dashboard. If RPC errors cross 2% or latency doubles, scale back to 0.5% and DM me and Ravi immediately."

Exact commands / quick pins (copyable):
- Pin image in rollout-config: curl -X POST $ORCH/api/v1/pin -d '{\"service\":\"runtime\",\"tag\":\"v2025-11-04-rc3\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Update router rule: gh api repos/redwood-inference/router/contents/canary-rules --input - <<'EOF' {\"patch\":\"replace cohort match for header X-Launch-Cohort -> 0.005\"} EOF
- Start warmup: ./scripts/priming/kv_spinup.py --cohort 0.005 --duration 900

Safety knobs and fallbacks:
- Fallback model variant: v2025-10-stable (lower perf but wide testing). If configured, automatic route fallback is enabled (policy: fallback-to-stable).
- Token bucket throttle: if per-tenant cost delta > 50% over baseline, apply tenant-level slow-down until human review.
- Forced pin: platform-admin can force traffic to stable with 'orch rollback --force --tag v2025-10-stable' (requires two approvers).

Edge cases / gotchas I've seen:
- Clients without X-Launch-Cohort header still get fallback routing sometimes due to proxy caching; watch router hit histogram.
- SDK versions < 1.9.2 ignore cohort header — double-check known-client list (clients/locked-sdk.csv).
- Cold-starts: small canaries on large-context models will overrepresent cold-start latencies; flag as expected in the first 10m.

Post-rollout observation (first 6h):
- Check for model quality regressions: run the smoke eval set against live outputs (smoke-evals/quick-run) at 30m and 3h marks.
- Ask product to run a small manual QA pass on 50 samples from the canary window if available.
- Collect a token-sampled subset for drift checks and save to s3://redwood-release-samples/2025-11-04-canary/ (note retention rules).

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Add an automated mid-canary quality check (small eval-run) and tie it to progression gates (INF-3667 follow-up).
- [ ] Formalize the evening handoff snippet in the runbook (confluence).
- [ ] Add a small dashboard tile that shows cohort header propagation rate (router -> backend mismatch).

Escalation contacts (evening):
- Primary oncall: Ravi Patel (pager)
- Runtime SME: Maya Chen (Slack/DM)
- Release owner: Oliver Grant (pager backup)
- Security contact (if data anomaly): Priya Singh

Notes to self: keep this page short and copyable. Save a postmortem template here if anything goes wrong. If you add another shortcut command, paste it under the "Exact commands" section.

Session log snippets (for my memory):
- 18:05 start warmup -> warmup extended +10m due to cache hit-rate 58%
- 18:23 progressed to 2% -> slight P95 bump (~1.3x) but RPC err stayed at 0.3%
- 18:48 progressed to 8% -> saw model_token_errors x2 baseline, scaled back to 2% and opened INF-XXX investigation (TODO: create ticket)

Last edits: added forced-pin command and circuit-breaker thresholds (2026-03-10).
